details.label: Summary
details.text: The threat for damaging wind gusts may increase through late afternoon as the ongoing storms encounter a more unstable air mass

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Strong to potentially severe storms currently emerging from the Blue Ridge Mountains are moving into a hotter and more unstable air mass, characterized by MLCAPE of 2000-2500 J/kg and 0-3 km lapse rates of around 8 C/km. Moreover, The KLWX VWP is sampling strengthening westerly winds above 3.5 km AGL, which may aid in storm organization. The extent of the damaging wind threat will be dependent on the degree of cold-pool organization that can occur. However, the more favorable parameter space with eastward extent suggests that threat should increase through late afternoon

details.label: Summary
details.text: The potential for at least isolated damaging wind gusts may increase over the next one to two hours. Convective trends are being monitored for a possible severe thunderstorm watch

details.label: Discussion
details.text: A line of thunderstorms over central WV has recently shown a weakened trend, per volumetric radar data, with the associated cold pool moving south-southeast at 40-45 kt. Additional showers and thunderstorms are developing ahead of the gust front, and it's possible that activity could reinforce the cold pool, leading to the re-intensification of the thunderstorm line. That process may be aided by stronger heating across the downstream air mass where objective analysis indicates comparatively steeper low-level lapse rates with MLCAPE of 1500-2000 J/kg. Given the above considerations, the threat for at least isolated damaging wind gusts may increase over the next 1-2 hours. However, it's unclear whether sufficient storm organization will occur to warrant a severe thunderstorm watch

details.label: Summary
details.text: Portions of far east-central Iowa into northern Illinois are being monitored for some increase in severe-thunderstorm potential this afternoon. If sustained storms can evolve, severe wind gusts and large hail will both be possible

details.label: Discussion
details.text: The latest surface analysis and visible satellite imagery indicate a W/E-oriented stationary boundary extending from east-central IA across northern IL. The earlier 12Z ILX sounding sampled robust capping at the base of the EML, though temperatures are warming into the lower/middle 80s amid upper 70s dewpoints, and continued heating should further erode inhibition. Steep midlevel lapse rates accompanying the EML atop the rich PBL moisture is yielding strong to locally extreme surface-based buoyancy along the boundary. Isolated thunderstorms are evolving along the boundary in far east-central IA, where surface convergence is maximized. While remaining inhibition and generally weak large-scale forcing for ascent cast uncertainty on the longevity of this activity and the development of additional storms this afternoon, the aforementioned buoyancy and around 30-40 kt of effective shear will conditionally support organized storms including supercells. Any sustained storms will pose a risk of large hail and severe wind gusts. Currently, confidence in sustained storms is highest over eastern IA and vicinity, where some influence of large-scale forcing for ascent preceding an approaching midlevel wave is evident. The need for a watch is uncertain, though convective and environmental trends are being monitored
